external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes the nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

processes.name: supplier portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor datasheet says the platform is secure by design, that it uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: Loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where the supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_stores.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform is secure by design, that it uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review submissions
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection decisions

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance documents and staff contact details

data_flows.name: retrieve documents
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: System description states: "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The same source also states: "The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is." These are incompatible positive claims about encryption in transit.

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-hosted environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier portal presents a web interface because the source calls it a portal.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the system as a supplier portal.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's stored compliance documents and staff contact details are confidential because they contain personal and commercially sensitive information.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's supplier data extract is confidential because it contains supplier records and staff-related information.
assumptions.basis: The bucket receives a supplier data extract derived from the described supplier paperwork and contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's records are confidential because they contain supplier records and staff-related information.
assumptions.basis: The database stores records written from the supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The nightly extract's encryption-in-transit value is unresolved because the source gives incompatible claims: end-to-end encryption and arrival as a plain CSV.
assumptions.basis: The source says the extract is encrypted end to end, while the landing-bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV.
